metadata.case_name: NG HIU MAN v. TRADE IN ASIA LTD

injuries.description: Contusion and possible strain of the muscles of the lower back
source: the injury to her back is likely to be some kind of contusion and possible strain of the muscles of her lower back.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

injuries.description: Bulging of intervertebral discs at L2-S1 levels with mild nerve root compression at various levels; small annular tear at L3/L4; multiple levels disc degeneration L2-L5
source: The MRI report revealed bulging of intervertebral discs at L2-S1 levels with mild bilateral nerve root compression at L2/L3, mild left nerve root compression at L3/L4, and mild right nerve root compression at L4/L5.
the latest MRI of the plaintiff�s lumbar spine showed multiple levels disc degeneration without significant nerve root compression and it also showed a small annular tear at L3/L4 level.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of nerve root of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: Left lower limb numbness over anterior thigh, buttock and leg with intermittent attack
Intermittent attacks aggravated by prolonged sitting or standing for more than one hour, or lifting heavy object
Needs to use a stick for long journeys or journeys with prolonged walking for more than 30 minutes
No lower limb neurological deficit on clinical examination

source: she did not seek medical treatment until 31 July 2011 (Sunday) when she consulted a Chinese bonesetter for the first time. She went to the same bonesetter for the second time on 1 August 2011 (Monday).

treatments_received.treatment: Accident & Emergency attendance and treatment at Prince of Wales Hospital (A&E of PWH) on 3 August 2011
source: the plaintiff attended the Accident and Emergency Department of the Prince of Wales Hospital for consultation and treatment on 3 August 2011 (Wednesday).

According to the pro forma medical report of Dr Ma Kwok Ping of the A&E of PWH dated 4 January 2012, the plaintiff attended the A&E of PWH at 10:47 pm on 3 August 2011 for "injury(ies) allegedly sustained ... 'Back sprain 3 days before'"

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations with private doctors (Town Health Medical Centre; Dr Edmund Wong of Hong Kong Traumatology and Orthopaedics Institute; Ever Health Medical Center)
source: she consulted Dr Ho Sie Kiu of the Town Health Medical Centre (康健醫務中心), a private medical doctor, on 8 August 2011.
Starting from 12 August 2011 and until 20 September 2011, the plaintiff consulted Dr Edmund Wong of the Hong Kong Traumatology and Orthopaedics Institute 6 times.
the plaintiff consulted Dr Wong Ping Kin, Raymond of Ever Health Medical Center on 10 October 2011.
She was also referred to a physiotherapist and received 3 sessions of physiotherapy treatment between this period between 18 August 2011 and 15 September 2011.
During the period from 13 October 2011 to 1 February 2012, the plaintiff attended 9 sessions of physiotherapy but had defaulted 6 appointments.

treatments_received.treatment: MRI scan in Mainland China on 18 September 2011
source: she had a MRI scan done in Mainland China on 18 September 2011. The MRI report revealed bulging of intervertebral discs at L2-S1 levels with mild bilateral nerve root compression at L2/L3, mild left nerve root compression at L3/L4, and mild right nerve root compression at L4/L5.

treatments_received.treatment: A&E attendance on 27 September 2011 and referral to Orthopaedics & Traumatology (PWH)
source: Upon the expiry of the sick leave period granted by Dr Edmund Wong on 26 September 2011, the plaintiff sought medical treatment at the A&E of PWH again on 27 September 2011. She was treated and discharged with 10 days sick leave from 27 September 2011 to 6 October 2011.

The plaintiff was referred to orthopaedic specialists for further medical information. Initial screening of the plaintiff was done by the Physiotherapy Department of PWH on 28 September 2011 and a report on her condition was made and sent to the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology, PWH for follow up.

treatments_received.treatment: Attendance at Department of Family Medicine & General Outpatient Clinic in Tai Po (OPC) with sick leave
source: the plaintiff attended the Department of Family Medicine & General Outpatient Clinic in Tai Po ("the OPC") for consultation on 7 October 2011 and was granted sick leave from 7 to 10 October 2011.
When her sick leave expired on 14 October 2011, the plaintiff went back to the OPC for consultation again on 14 October 2011 ... and she was given 4 days of sick leave from 15 to 18 October 2011.

treatments_received.treatment: Management by Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology, PWH (24 October 2011 to 3 May 2012) with long sick leave and multidisciplinary follow-up
source: On 24 October 2011, the plaintiff attended the O&T of PWH as scheduled for consultation. According to the relevant medical report, during the period between 24 October 2011 and 3 May 2012 the plaintiff's case was managed by the O&T of PWH and sick leave of almost 8 months was granted to her from 24 October 2011 to 14 June 2012.

During this period when the plaintiff was covered by the long sick leave granted by the O&T of PWH, she was also given appointments by the Physiotherapy Department, Occupational Therapy Department, and the Pain Clinic of the Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital ("Nethersole Hospital") in Tai Po for the treatment and management of her conditions.

treatments_received.treatment: Pain Clinic follow-up at Nethersole Hospital (followed up for 4 months until 20 June 2012)
source: The plaintiff was seen by doctor of the Pain Clinic on 23 February 2012 and the doctor noted degeneration in multiple levels of her spine from her private MRI report. She was followed up in the Pain Clinic for 4 months until 20 June 2012.

treatments_received.treatment: Occupational therapy and work capacity evaluation; later work hardening training (6 sessions) from 8 May 2013 to 5 September 2013
source: the plaintiff was also referred to the Occupational Therapy Department of the Nethersole Hospital on 6 February 2012. According to the relevant Occupational Therapist report dated 8 November 2012, initial occupational therapy assessment of the plaintiff was done on 21 May 2012. ... She attended 6 sessions of work hardening training. The results showed that the plaintiff's physical capacities marginally matched her job demands. She was discharged on 5 September 2013 upon her request.

treatments_received.treatment: MRI scan at PWH on 26 February 2013
source: Shortly after the joint examination by the two experts, another MRI scan was done on the plaintiff in PWH on 26 February 2013.

losses.description: Activities of daily living and the use of public transportation were manageable but with some inconvenience; plaintiff claimed she would need to use a stick for long journeys or journeys with prolonged walking for more than 30 minutes.
Left lower limb numbness over anterior thigh, buttock and leg with intermittent attacks.
